subject.title: [Feature]: Allow job-level model override for cron jobs using sessionTarget=main + payload.kind=systemEvent

question: Should main-session `systemEvent` cron jobs gain their own model/provider override contract, and should that contract reuse `payload.model`, add top-level `model`/`provider`, or add an explicit `sessionOverride` block?
rationale: Current code intentionally treats `systemEvent` as text-only and main-session execution as a heartbeat/system-event enqueue; changing it affects public schema, stored cron jobs, session state, provider validation, and docs/UI behavior.

options.title: Add top-level cron override
options.body: Add job-level `model`/`provider` fields that apply across payload kinds and validate before enqueueing or waking.

options.title: Reuse payload.model
options.body: Extend `systemEvent` payloads with model/provider fields, accepting a narrower diff but mixing agent-turn-only fields into the text-event payload contract.

options.title: Defer main-session overrides
options.body: Keep main-systemEvent jobs text-only and document isolated/custom-session agentTurn as the supported per-job model path.

recommendation.title: Add top-level cron override
recommendation.body: Add job-level `model`/`provider` fields that apply across payload kinds and validate before enqueueing or waking.

likelyOwner.reason: The choice changes core cron/provider/session API semantics and needs maintainer product ownership beyond a narrow repair.
